title: Ezekiel Chapter 23 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 23 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 23 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 23.

questions.question: Who were the two women mentioned in Ezekiel 23?
questions.explanation: The two women mentioned are named Aholah and Aholibah, as stated in Ezekiel 23:4.

questions.question: True or False: Aholah is described as the younger sister.
questions.explanation: Aholah is referred to as the elder sister in Ezekiel 23:4.

questions.question: Which group did Aholah doted on?
questions.explanation: Aholah played the harlot and doted on her lovers, specifically the Assyrians, as mentioned in Ezekiel 23:5.

questions.question: True or False: Aholibah was less corrupt than Aholah.
questions.explanation: Aholibah was more corrupt in her love and whoredoms than Aholah, according to Ezekiel 23:11.

questions.question: What did Aholah do with the Assyrians?
questions.explanation: Aholah committed her whoredoms with the Assyrians, as stated in Ezekiel 23:7.

questions.question: True or False: Aholibah was attracted to the Chaldeans.
questions.explanation: Aholibah doted upon the Chaldeans, as described in Ezekiel 23:14-16.

questions.question: What did Aholah not leave behind from Egypt?
questions.explanation: Aholah did not leave her whoredoms brought from Egypt, as stated in Ezekiel 23:8.

questions.question: Who came to Aholah into the bed of love?
questions.explanation: The Babylonians came to Aholah into the bed of love, as mentioned in Ezekiel 23:17.

questions.question: True or False: Aholah experienced alienation from her lovers.
questions.explanation: Aholah's mind was alienated from her lovers after she defiled herself with them, according to Ezekiel 23:17.

questions.question: Which of the following describes Aholah's lovers?
questions.explanation: Aholah's lovers are described as desirable young men, specifically the Assyrians, in Ezekiel 23:6.

questions.question: What did the Assyrians do to Aholah?
questions.explanation: The Assyrians discovered Aholah's nakedness and executed judgment upon her, leading to her becoming famous among women, as stated in Ezekiel 23:10.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 23, which event occurs first?
questions.explanation: Aholah's whoredoms in Egypt are mentioned before other events, as stated in Ezekiel 23:3.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 23 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 23 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Aholibah do after seeing Aholah's fate?
questions.explanation: Aholibah saw Aholah's fate and became more corrupt in her inordinate love than Aholah, as stated in Ezekiel 23:11.

questions.question: What will happen to Aholibah's lovers according to the Lord?
options: They will be kind to her
They will be raised against her
questions.correctAnswer: They will be raised against her
questions.explanation: The Lord declares that He will raise up Aholibah's lovers against her, as mentioned in Ezekiel 23:22.

questions.question: True or False: Aholibah did not remember the whoredoms of her youth.
questions.explanation: Aholibah multiplied her whoredoms by remembering the days of her youth, as described in Ezekiel 23:19.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 23, how did Aholibah react to the images of the Chaldeans?
questions.explanation: Aholibah saw men portrayed on the wall and doted upon the images of the Chaldeans, as stated in Ezekiel 23:14-16.

questions.question: What does the Lord say He will do because Aholibah has gone a whoring after the heathen?
questions.explanation: The Lord will bring judgment upon Aholibah because she has gone a whoring after the heathen and is polluted with their idols, as stated in Ezekiel 23:30.

questions.question: True or False: The Babylonians and the Chaldeans are described as desirable young men.
questions.explanation: The Babylonians and Chaldeans are described as desirable young men, as mentioned in Ezekiel 23:23.

questions.question: What will happen to Aholibah's children according to the judgment described?
questions.explanation: The judgment states that Aholibah's sons and daughters will be taken away, as indicated in Ezekiel 23:25.

questions.question: What is the significance of drinking from the sister's cup as mentioned in Ezekiel 23?
questions.explanation: Drinking from the sister's cup signifies that Aholibah will experience the same fate as her sister Aholah, which is a punishment, as per Ezekiel 23:32.

questions.question: How does this passage demonstrate the consequences of idolatry?
questions.explanation: The passage illustrates that engaging in idolatry and whoredoms leads to severe consequences and judgment from God, as highlighted throughout Ezekiel 23.

questions.question: True or False: Aholibah's lewdness will be made to cease.
questions.explanation: The Lord states He will make Aholibah's lewdness cease, as indicated in Ezekiel 23:27.

questions.question: What does the Lord say will happen to Aholibah's garments and jewels?
questions.explanation: The Lord says that Aholibah will be stripped of her clothes and jewels, as per Ezekiel 23:26.

questions.question: What was Aholibah’s attitude towards her lovers according to the text?
questions.explanation: Aholibah is described as doting on her lovers, indicating a strong desire, as stated in Ezekiel 23:12.

questions.question: What actions did Aholibah take to prepare for her lovers according to the text?
questions.explanation: Aholibah washed herself and painted her eyes to prepare for her lovers, as mentioned in Ezekiel 23:40.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 23, what is a consequence of forgetting the Lord?
questions.explanation: The passage reveals that forgetting the Lord leads to bearing the consequences of one's lewdness and whoredoms, as stated in Ezekiel 23:35.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 23 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 23.

questions.question: What was Aholah's relationship to Aholibah?
questions.explanation: Aholah and Aholibah are described as sisters, the daughters of one mother (Ezekiel 23:2).

questions.question: Who did Aholah play the harlot with?
questions.explanation: Aholah is stated to have played the harlot with the Assyrians her neighbors (Ezekiel 23:5).

questions.question: What did Aholibah do when she saw what happened to Aholah?
questions.explanation: Aholibah saw Aholah's fate and became more corrupt in her love and whoredoms (Ezekiel 23:11).

questions.question: What did the Lord say He would bring against Aholibah?
questions.explanation: The Lord said He would raise up Aholibah's lovers against her (Ezekiel 23:22).

questions.question: What did Aholibah use to prepare for her lovers?
questions.explanation: Aholibah prepared a table with incense and oil for her lovers (Ezekiel 23:41).

questions.question: True or False: Aholah and Aholibah are described in the chapter as faithful to God.
questions.explanation: Both Aholah and Aholibah committed whoredoms and were unfaithful, as stated throughout the chapter.

questions.question: How did Aholibah respond to the images of the Chaldeans?
questions.explanation: Aholibah doted upon the images of the Chaldeans when she saw them drawn on the wall (Ezekiel 23:14).

questions.question: Which group is mentioned as one of Aholibah's lovers?
questions.explanation: The Babylonians are explicitly mentioned as coming to Aholibah (Ezekiel 23:17).

questions.question: What did the Lord say would be the fate of Aholibah?
questions.explanation: The Lord declared judgment upon Aholibah, stating that they shall stone them with stones and slay their sons and daughters (Ezekiel 23:47).

questions.question: True or False: The chapter states that Aholah and Aholibah had committed adultery and caused their children to pass through the fire.
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that they committed adultery and caused their sons to pass through the fire (Ezekiel 23:37).

questions.question: What is one of the consequences mentioned for Aholibah due to her lewdness?
options: She would be given a new land
She would be delivered into the hands of her enemies
She would be blessed with prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: She would be delivered into the hands of her enemies
questions.explanation: The Lord states He will deliver Aholibah into the hand of those whom she hates (Ezekiel 23:28).

questions.question: Which verse indicates that the Lord would make lewdness cease out of the land?
questions.explanation: The Lord declares that He will cause lewdness to cease out of the land (Ezekiel 23:48).

questions.question: In what way does Ezekiel 23 connect with the theme of idolatry found in other parts of the Bible?
options: It shows God's mercy towards idolaters
It illustrates the consequences of turning away from God
It ignores the issue of idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the consequences of turning away from God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel's portrayal of Aholah and Aholibah's idolatry aligns with themes in other books, such as the warnings in Jeremiah and Isaiah regarding the consequences of idolatry.

questions.question: What Hebrew word is used in the chapter to describe the act of whoredom, and what does it imply in a broader sense?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'zanah' is used to describe whoredom, indicating a breach of covenant and fidelity, which relates to idolatry as a form of spiritual adultery.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 23 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 23 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 23 reveal about the consequences of idolatry and sin?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:25 indicates that God will set His jealousy against them, leading to severe consequences including violence and loss. This demonstrates that idolatry results in divine judgment.

questions.question: What characterizes the relationship between Aholah and the Assyrians as described in Ezekiel 23?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:5 states that Aholah played the harlot and doted on her lovers, indicating her unfaithfulness to God.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is displayed in His response to the actions of Aholah and Aholibah?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 23:25, God expresses jealousy towards Aholah and Aholibah due to their unfaithfulness, demonstrating His concern for His holiness and relationship with His people.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 23:39 indicate about the actions taken by Aholah and Aholibah?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:39 states that they have defiled God's sanctuary and profaned His sabbaths, clearly indicating their engagement in idolatrous practices.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 23 connect to the broader narrative of Israel's unfaithfulness?
options: It highlights the theme of covenant unfaithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the theme of covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23 illustrates Israel's repeated unfaithfulness through the metaphor of Aholah and Aholibah, which reflects the overarching theme of Israel's covenantal failure throughout Scripture.

questions.question: What lesson about divine judgment can be drawn from Ezekiel 23:47?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:47 describes the dire consequences of Aholah and Aholibah's actions, emphasizing that divine judgment will come as a result of their unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 23:20 reveal about Aholibah's desires?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:20 indicates that Aholibah doted upon her paramours, showing her desires were directed towards her sinful relationships rather than towards God.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 11 and 18 convey about Aholibah's character?
options: She was more corrupt than Aholah
She was indifferent to her lovers
questions.correctAnswer: She was more corrupt than Aholah
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:11 shows that Aholibah was more corrupt in her love than Aholah, while Ezekiel 23:18 reveals that God’s mind was alienated from her due to her continued unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 23:32 reflect on the nature of divine retribution?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:32 indicates that Aholibah will drink from her sister's cup, which represents the judgment that is justly given due to her actions.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 23:24 teach about the approach of Aholibah's enemies?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:24 describes how the enemies will come against Aholibah with chariots and judgment, indicating a direct confrontation due to her sins.

questions.question: What does the mention of the Babylonians in Ezekiel 23 signify regarding judgment?
options: They were instruments of God's judgment
They were a sign of peace
questions.correctAnswer: They were instruments of God's judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:23 lists the Babylonians as part of the judgment coming against Aholibah, signifying their role as instruments in executing God's judgment for her unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 23:22 indicate about the consequences faced by Aholibah?
options: She will be judged by her lovers
questions.correctAnswer: She will be judged by her lovers
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:22 says that God will raise up Aholibah's lovers against her, highlighting the principle that those who engage in sin will face consequences from those they have wronged.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 23:37 highlight about the nature of their sins?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:37 indicates that they committed adultery and caused their children to pass through the fire, showing the severity of their sins involving bloodshed and idolatry.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the Old Testament portrays God as unloving and harsh. What does Ezekiel 23:36-39 actually teach?
options: God seeks to restore His people
God's judgment is based on love and justice
God does not care about worship
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is based on love and justice
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23:36-39 emphasizes God's desire for holiness and how He responds to the unfaithfulness of His people, demonstrating that His judgments are rooted in justice and a desire for a faithful relationship.

questions.question: What overarching theme does Ezekiel 23 present regarding God's relationship with His people?
options: God desires fidelity and punishes unfaithfulness
God's love is unconditional regardless of actions
questions.correctAnswer: God desires fidelity and punishes unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 23 consistently illustrates the metaphor of marital unfaithfulness, demonstrating that God desires fidelity from His people and will respond with judgment when they stray.
